source.title: From Tempered to Benign Overfitting in ReLU Neural Networks
source.authors: Guy Kornowski; Gilad Yehudai; Ohad Shamir

page_placements.theme: Spectral, dimensional and signal conditions for benign or harmful interpolation

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies generalization of interpolating ReLU networks under label noise, but does not test or rely on the double-descent claim or any listed version of it.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error results about tempered, benign, and catastrophic overfitting, including effects of input dimension and label noise. These are recorded as findings that fit no listed version. It does not sweep model size, training epochs, or sample size to test a double-descent curve. The empirical plots report averages over runs; they are not numerical tests of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper studies whether interpolating 2-layer ReLU networks overfit in a tempered, benign or catastrophic way, as a function of input dimension and label noise. It never sweeps model size, epochs or sample size across an interpolation threshold, and never reports a test-error peak. Belkin et al. 2019 and other double-descent papers appear only in the related-work citations. The width comparison (n=50 vs 3000, Fig. 2 left) uses only widths that already interpolate, so it says nothing about a peak near the threshold (V1). Error rising with label noise is a related construct, not a noise-driven double-descent peak (V6). 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses', since double descent is not discussed beyond citations.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that, for 2-layer ReLU networks converging to max-margin KKT points, overfitting is tempered in one dimension and benign in high dimension. Experiments suggest a gradual transition as dimension grows relative to sample size, and width matters little once the network interpolates. Without biases, catastrophic or non-benign overfitting can occur.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies noisy-label interpolation and clean test error as a function of input dimension and noise, using theoretical max-margin analyses and SGD experiments. It does not use the original double-descent size, epoch, or sample-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported overfitting profile varies with input dimension and label-noise level. The paper also discusses dependence on bias terms and compares network widths and depth empirically.

fits_no_version.finding: In d=1, clean test error of any KKT-point interpolator lies between order p^5 and order √p. At a local minimum of the max-margin problem it scales linearly in p, independent of width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolating ReLU networks with low-dimensional inputs overfit in a tempered way, with clean error scaling with label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: With d of order at least m^2, under norm or KKT assumptions, clean test error is at most ϵ, decaying exponentially with d. Without bias terms, lower bounds and constructed KKT points give catastrophic or non-benign error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input dimension and bias terms determine whether interpolating ReLU networks overfit benignly or catastrophically.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD experiments show a gradual tempered-to-benign shift as d grows relative to m. Width (50 vs 3000) barely changes the plots, and depth 3 looks similar to depth 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overfitting profile depends on the input dimension to sample size ratio, not on width once the network interpolates.

record.problems: The empirical results are presented in plots without numerical values in the text. The high-dimensional theoretical results require specific assumptions about dimension, noise, parameter norm or output weights; the paper notes limitations of these assumptions.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep across the interpolation threshold. Widths compared (50, 3000) all interpolate.
No test error over training time is reported. The only epoch remark is that 100k epochs left results unchanged.
No sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold. m=500 vs m=2000 compares overfitting profiles, not a peak.
Clean test error grows with label noise p, but no double-descent peak, multiple descent or regularization is studied.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none'] with state cannot_determine. Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise double descent and the location of a peak near interpolation.
Whether increasing sample size near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
General double descent across model classes.
Whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
Whether noise drives a double-descent peak, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes them.
Whether effective parameter counting converts second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

tranche.reason: Studies clean test error versus label noise and input dimension among interpolating networks. Neither establishes a double-descent curve nor tests another listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Section 5 qualifies the transition: clean test error remains significantly above zero near p = 0.5 even at the highest tested dimensions. The supplied text is arXiv v3, dated March 2024.
